_comment: VV/VH anisotropy, native emtk windows. Drawn by emtk.view_form over AnisotropyModel (gui/model.py): 'controls' is the top window, 'batch' the batch window. The plots, the file dialogs, Help and Guide are drawn by gui/app.py.
title: VV/VH Anisotropy Decay

sections.title: VV/VH anisotropy
sections.name: controls
sections.description: Load a VV/VH file, set the correction and choose the region that defines r-infinity.

sections.text: Deprecated: VV/VH Anisotropy Decay is deprecated/obsolete. Use the VV/VH G-Factor plugin and reader-integrated anisotropy workflow instead.
sections.description: This tool is obsolete; the VV/VH G-Factor plugin and the reader-integrated anisotropy workflow replace it.
Load a VV/VH file, save the results, or process many files with the same settings.

buttons.label: Load VV/VH file…
buttons.description: Load a paired parallel/perpendicular decay (.dat or .txt, VV followed by VH). Dropping a file on the window does the same.

buttons.label: Save outputs…
buttons.description: Save the shifted VV/VH decays (<name>_shifted.dat), the anisotropy trace (<name>_anisotropy.txt: channel, r(t), r(t) minus r-infinity) and the r-infinity metadata (<name>_rinf.csv).

buttons.label: Batch files…
buttons.description: Open the batch window: queue many VV/VH files and compute r-infinity for each with the current settings.

sections.label: File
sections.description: The VV/VH file that is loaded.

sections.title: Correction
sections.description: Settings applied to VV and VH before r(t) = (VV - g VH) / (VV + 2 g VH) is formed.

sections.label: G-factor
sections.description: Detector sensitivity correction applied to VH (0 to 10).

sections.label: Apply backgrounds
sections.description: Subtract constant VV and VH backgrounds before calculation.

sections.label: BG VV
sections.description: Constant background to subtract from VV.

sections.label: BG VH
sections.description: Constant background to subtract from VH.

sections.label: Flip VV↔VH
sections.description: Swap channels when the source file has reversed polarization (data swapped in VV/VH).

sections.label: Shift VH (channels)
sections.description: Shift VH by a fractional channel using interpolation (-150 to 150).

sections.title: r-infinity region
sections.description: The channels whose r(t) is averaged to r-infinity. The two green lines in the anisotropy plot move the same bounds.

sections.label: Region start
sections.description: First channel in the r-infinity averaging region.

sections.label: Region end
sections.description: Last boundary of the r-infinity averaging region.

sections.label: r∞
sections.description: r-infinity: the mean of r(t) over the region, five decimals; N/A when there is no valid point in it.
What was loaded or saved, or why an action failed.

sections.title: VV/VH Anisotropy Batch Processor
sections.name: batch
sections.description: Compute r-infinity for many VV/VH files with one set of settings.
Queue VV/VH files, folders or database datasets, or take them off the queue.

buttons.label: Files
buttons.description: Queue VV/VH files (.dat or .txt). Dropping files on the window does the same.

buttons.label: Folder
buttons.description: Queue the .dat and .txt files of a folder, recursively.

buttons.label: Database
buttons.description: Select VV/VH datasets from the session MMFDB database.

buttons.label: Remove
buttons.description: Remove the selected file from the queue (it stays on disk).

buttons.label: Clear
buttons.description: Empty the queue and its results.

sections.description: The queued VV/VH files, in the order they are processed. Click a row to select it; Delete removes it.

columns.title: Path
columns.tooltip: The full path of the file.

sections.description: Run the batch with the settings the window was opened with, or save its table.

buttons.label: Run Batch
buttons.description: Compute r-infinity for each queued VV/VH file with the settings that were current when this window opened. A file that cannot be read gets a row with its error.

buttons.label: Save CSV…
buttons.description: Save the results table as CSV: filename, r_inf, region_min, region_max, bg_vv, bg_vh, g_factor, error.

buttons.label: Close
buttons.description: Close the batch window; the queue and the results are kept.

sections.description: One row per processed file: r-infinity, the region actually used (clamped to the file) and the settings.

columns.title: r_inf
columns.tooltip: Mean of r(t) over the region; NaN when the file could not be read.

columns.title: region_min
columns.tooltip: Lower region bound, clamped to the file's channels.

columns.title: region_max
columns.tooltip: Upper region bound, clamped to the file's channels.

columns.title: error
columns.tooltip: Why the file could not be read; empty when it was.

sections.description: What was queued, processed or saved, or why an action failed.
